name: Update WooCommerce sale prices from Amazon competitor data with Bright Data, GPT-5.6 and Slack

parameters.content:
## Move your WooCommerce prices when Amazon moves

Point it at your shop and a sheet of SKU to Amazon URL pairs. It reads the buy-box price for each, checks the two are the same product, and writes a new sale price back to WooCommerce.

### How it works
A daily schedule reads your products from WooCommerce and your SKU map from Google Sheets, then sends the Amazon URLs to Bright Data's product dataset. It polls the snapshot on a Wait loop until the rows are ready.

GPT-5.6 confirms each pair is the same product before anything is priced, because a wrong URL in the sheet looks exactly like a bargain. Only the buy-box price is read - the other-sellers list mixes in used warehouse units.

Then the guardrails: never below your cost plus margin, never above the regular price, never further than max_change_percent in one run, and anything outside 0.4x to 2.5x of your price is treated as a bad match rather than an opportunity. Everything held back is named in the digest with its reason.

It writes the **sale** price, not the regular price, so clearing it puts the shop back where it started. Prices move both ways, inside the same cap.

### Setup
Add a Bright Data API key as a Header Auth credential (`Authorization` / `Bearer YOUR_KEY`), connect WooCommerce, Google Sheets, OpenAI and Slack, then set your sheet ID in Set Repricing Rules. The sheet needs `sku`, `amazon_url` and `cost` columns.

### Customization
`dry_run` ships on, so the first run reports and changes nothing. Tune `undercut_percent`, `min_margin_percent` and `max_change_percent` to taste. Three optional add-ons sit unwired beside the main chain: clear today's sale prices to roll a run back, mail the digest instead of posting it, or hold named promo SKUs out of the run.

## 1. The shop and the map
Products come from WooCommerce, and a sheet of SKU to Amazon URL pairs says what each one competes with.

## 2. Read Amazon asynchronously
Bright Data returns the buy-box price per URL. Four products took nine seconds in testing, so this polls the snapshot until the rows are ready.

## 3. Confirm it is the same product
A wrong URL in the sheet looks exactly like a bargain, so the two titles are checked before any price is worked out.

## 4. Apply the guardrails
Cost floor, regular price ceiling, a cap on how far one run can move, and a sanity band that rejects prices too far from yours.

## 5. Preview or write
With `dry_run` on, the write is skipped and the digest still says exactly what would have changed.

## 6. Log and tell the team
One sheet row per price change, plus a digest that names everything held back and why.

## Optional add-ons
Not wired up. Roll a run back, email the digest instead of Slack, or hold promo SKUs out.

## This one writes to your shop

`dry_run` is on by default and the first run changes nothing. Leave it on until you have read a digest and checked the held-back list - a wrong `amazon_url` in the sheet is the one mistake the guardrails cannot fully catch.
